data.title: Conduent Reaches Class Action Cybersecurity Settlement Agreement
data.description:
The latest update is out from Conduent ( (CNDT) ).

On October 16, 2026, Conduent and certain subsidiaries entered into a Class Action Settlement Agreement to resolve a consolidated class action lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey arising from a January 2025 cybersecurity incident. The agreement, which remains subject to court approval, follows earlier disclosure of the data breach and is structured to bring closure to litigation stemming from that event.

Under the Settlement Agreement, Conduent will contribute $80 million to a non-reversionary fund covering class member recoveries, credit and medical data monitoring, plaintiffs’ counsel fees and settlement administration costs, representing its total monetary obligation under the deal. The settlement, which Conduent emphasizes is not an admission of fault, will release the company, affected clients and those clients’ customers from claims related to the incident, and Conduent says existing cyber insurance means it does not expect a material impact on its financial position, operating results or cash flows.

data.title: XTI Aerospace Faces Default Waivers and Debt Restructuring
data.description:
The latest update is out from XTI Aerospace ( (XTIA) ).

On November 10, 2025, XTI Drones Holdings issued two seller promissory notes totaling nearly $12 million to finance the acquisitions of Drone Nerds and Anzu Robotics, with interest originally set at 7.25% and final maturity on November 10, 2026. Required principal installments of $1.38 million under the Drone Nerds note and $120,000 under the Anzu Robotics note, due by September 30, 2026, were not paid.

Because those missed payments were not cured within ten days, events of default were triggered under both notes on October 11, 2026, when the aggregate outstanding principal, including capitalized interest, stood at about $4.51 million. The default raised interest to 9.25% and gave the note holders the right to accelerate all amounts due, although as of the latest filing they had not exercised these remedies.
